source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: block image read (Irish News, 30 April 1936, p. 7, section 2.153 block 3): 'The divisions in which no nominations were received are Somerset and Drumcroon, but it is expected that the two outgoing members, Messrs. John N. Henry and Matthew Workman, respectively, will continue in office'; John N. Henry was returned for Somerset in 1933

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received by Mr. S. Hezlett, clerk of the Union and returning officer, on 28 April 1936; all the outgoing councillors except two were re-nominated, and a contest was likely only in Lislea (Kilrea), where Mr. John Torrens opposed the outgoing councillor, Mr. John R. Gordon, J.P. (Irish News, 30 April 1936, p. 7; Belfast News-Letter, 30 April 1936, p. 9). No nomination was received for Somerset, and the outgoing member, John N. Henry, was expected to 'continue in office', that is, he was deemed re-elected. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
